sections.h2: Masonry is not drywall, and it is not wood
body: Concrete masonry units, poured concrete, and brick are porous, alkaline, and full of moisture they pick up from rain and the ground. That makes them durable but tricky to paint. Concrete block painting done with ordinary exterior paint tends to look pitted, absorb water through the pores, and fail early. Masonry needs its own system.

We paint unstuccoed block homes and additions, garden and privacy walls, retaining walls, utility buildings, commercial block warehouses, brick homes, and concrete columns and soffits. Garage and shop floors are a separate specialty, covered on our garage floor epoxy coating page.

New concrete and fresh mortar are strongly alkaline. The wrong primer gets attacked chemically and lets go within months, a failure called saponification. That is why new block needs adequate cure time and an alkali-resistant primer. We check the age of the work and the manufacturer's guidance before scheduling.

Older walls have a different enemy: efflorescence, the white crystalline powder left when moisture moves through masonry and deposits salts on the surface. Painting over it guarantees peeling. It has to be cleaned off, the wall allowed to dry, and the moisture source addressed, whether that is a missing cap, soil piled against the wall, or irrigation hitting it daily.

sections.h2: Block filler: the step that separates pros from paint jobs
body: Bare CMU is full of pinholes and open pores. Roll paint straight on and it bridges some and misses others, leaving a speckled film that lets water in. Block filler is a thick, high-solids primer worked into the face of the block so every void is closed and the topcoat forms a continuous skin.

It takes more material and labor, which is exactly why it gets skipped on cheap bids. Leaving it out shortens the job by a day and the life of the coating by years. On our estimates block filler is a named line item with the product listed, so you can see whether competing bids include it.

Masonry topcoats need to block liquid water while letting vapor escape. Depending on the wall, that means a premium 100% acrylic masonry paint, a high-build coating, or an elastomeric where hairline cracking is present. We use Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore lines and apply two full coats, back-rolling sprayed coats into the texture.

Brick is its own conversation. Painted brick needs breathable products, and many owners now prefer limewash, a mineral finish that soaks into the brick and weathers softly. That option is covered on our decorative and limewash finishes page. If a wall has a leak problem rather than a looks problem, our waterproofing and protective coatings service is the better starting point.
bullets: Alkali-resistant masonry primer on new or bare concrete
Two coats of breathable acrylic, high-build, or elastomeric topcoat

body: Each surface gets a slightly different system. A freshly built block garden wall needs cure time and an alkali-resistant primer before anything else; a thirty-year-old block home with chalky paint needs washing, a bonding primer over the old film, and filler only where bare block shows. Poured concrete columns and tilt-wall panels are smoother and may skip filler but still need a masonry primer. Retaining walls need special attention to the back side and weep holes, because water pushing through from the soil will lift any coating on the face.
For commercial block buildings, see our warehouse and industrial painting service, where masonry coatings are scheduled around loading and operating hours.

Prep starts with a thorough pressure or soft wash to strip dirt, mildew, and chalking paint. Loose coatings are scraped back, cracks are filled with masonry-grade patch or sealant, and efflorescence is treated. Moisture readings confirm the wall is dry enough to coat. Block buildings with stucco on some elevations are handled together with our stucco repair and painting crews so the system matches.

Exterior masonry is best painted October through May, and summer work starts early to stay ahead of afternoon storms. Commercial block buildings can be scheduled around operating hours. Your estimate lists primer, filler, topcoat, coats, and schedule in writing.

Once coated, masonry needs little more than an occasional wash to keep mildew from taking hold on shaded faces. Keep irrigation heads aimed away from walls and soil pulled back from the base so the wall can dry. Labelled touch-up paint is left with you, and exterior work carries a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years in addition to the manufacturer's coverage.

faqs.q: Do I really need block filler?
faqs.a: On open-textured CMU, yes. It closes pinholes so the topcoat forms a continuous waterproof film. Without it, the wall looks speckled and absorbs water.

faqs.q: How long should new block cure before painting?
faqs.a: It depends on the product and conditions, so we follow the primer manufacturer's guidance. The key is that new masonry is very alkaline and needs both cure time and an alkali-resistant primer.

faqs.q: What is the white powder on my painted block wall?
faqs.a: That is efflorescence, salt carried to the surface by moisture moving through the wall. It must be cleaned and the moisture source corrected before repainting.
Yes, with breathable masonry products. Many owners choose limewash instead, which gives a softer, mineral look and will not peel the way a film coating can.
